pairs.subject: fleet-orchestration
pairs.evidence: src/lib/org/followups.ts:162 A craft row that the rescan does not restate is closed as done on its Ascent-Resolves trailer alone. For the lane, that trailer is written from the ids the session itself reported resolved (followups.ts:454), so the worker's claim becomes the ruling with no artifact check, and the case is not reported as UNVERIFIED. This contradicts the header of followup-claims.ts, which says done needs the dimension to move.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/org/followups.ts:162 The gap path needs attributable movement, but the craft path closes on the delegate's own claim. A case nothing can verify should be held as UNVERIFIED, not passed as done.
src/lib/org/followups.ts:274 Every lane prompt restates the worker's capability limits and the void rules inside the brief itself; it does not assume the worker loaded any standing files.
src/lib/mcp/work-tools.ts:351 Failure and escalation are first-class reported results. A 'resolved' report only clears the lease and leaves the ruling to the rescan.
src/lib/db/followup-claims.ts:191 There is one claim door, arbitrated by a database compare-and-set, so a row can never have two concurrent holders. A held row is refused, never stolen.
src/lib/db/followup-claims.ts:112 Alongside the report_attempt signals, a lazy sweeper releases lapsed leases with a vocabulary of its own ('lease expired'), not as success.

pairs.registryProposal: completion-claim-verification could name the case where the acceptance instrument (here, a scoring rubric) structurally cannot witness the work. In that case the corpus should say the claim stays UNVERIFIED and counted apart, not promoted to done because the alternative would stall a ladder.
